name: Astronaut
description: Flies a spacecraft and runs scientific experiments in weightlessness, living for weeks or months on an orbital station. Before a flight comes long training: the ship's systems, medicine and working in a spacesuit.
fact: Before launching from Baikonur, Russian cosmonauts traditionally watch the film "White Sun of the Desert".

name: Pilot
description: Flies the aircraft together with a first officer, watches the instruments and stays in constant contact with controllers on the ground. Goes through regular medical checks and simulator training to be ready for anything out of the ordinary.
fact: Before every flight, pilots have to attend a briefing and check the aircraft against a strict checklist.

name: Surgeon
description: Operates on organs and tissue to deal with injuries, tumours and birth defects that drugs cannot cure. Works in a sterile operating theatre alongside an anaesthetist and assistants, sometimes for many hours at a stretch.
fact: Before an operation surgeons scrub their hands through several strict stages and put on sterile gloves and gown.

name: Dentist
description: Treats teeth and gums, puts in fillings, crowns and braces, and keeps an eye on the health of the whole mouth. At the chair a drill, a mirror and dozens of small instruments allow precise work in a very tight space.
fact: Fear of the dentist is one of the most common phobias in the world, and it even has its own name: dentophobia.

name: Veterinarian
description: Treats pets and farm animals, makes diagnoses without a word from the patient and operates on creatures of every size, from a hamster to a horse. Also gives vaccinations and looks after the health of animals on farms and in zoos.
fact: Many vets specialise in a single kind of animal, working only with birds, reptiles or horses.

name: Firefighter
description: Puts out fires and pulls people out of flames, smoke and rubble, and is also called out to crashes, floods and other emergencies. Works in heavy gear and a breathing apparatus, often in high heat and almost no visibility.
fact: Firefighters check their engines and equipment at the start of every shift, so they can roll out within minutes.

name: Police officer
description: Enforces the law, patrols the streets, sorts out conflicts and investigates offences. Works in uniform and in plain view of the public, so has to combine firmness with the ability to talk people down under stress.
fact: Uniforms and powers differ from country to country — in some places officers are on duty without firearms by default.

name: Private investigator
description: Gathers information and runs enquiries for private clients or companies, from tracing missing people to checking on unfaithful spouses and corporate fraud. Unlike the police, works within civil rather than criminal powers.
fact: The image of the detective with a pipe and a magnifying glass largely comes from fiction — the real work is mostly archives and surveillance.

name: Judge
description: Hears cases in court and delivers judgments on the basis of the law and the evidence put forward by the parties. Has to stay impartial and justify every sentence or ruling by reference to specific rules of law.
fact: In some countries judges wear special robes and wigs, a tradition that goes back to the British courts of the 17th century.

name: Lawyer
description: Defends a client's interests in court and outside it: drafts contracts, gives legal advice and builds a line of defence or prosecution. Needs a sound knowledge of the law and the ability to argue a position convincingly to judge and jury.
fact: Legal privilege means a lawyer cannot disclose what a client has told them, even if investigators demand it.

name: Head chef
description: Runs a restaurant kitchen, invents the menu and makes sure every plate comes out equally perfect. Beyond cooking, is responsible for buying produce, training the cooks and keeping order in the kitchen during the busiest service.
fact: The tall white chef's hat is called a toque, and by tradition its height showed the cook's place in the kitchen hierarchy.

name: Bartender
description: Mixes cocktails, pours drinks and sets the mood behind the bar, often ending up somewhere between a conversationalist and a therapist for the customers. Has to remember dozens of recipes and work fast through the evening rush.
fact: The art of tossing and spinning shakers and bottles for show is called flair bartending.

name: Sommelier
description: Matches wine to dishes, advises restaurant guests and looks after the wine list and the conditions the bottles are kept in. Can name the grape variety, the region and roughly the vintage by smell and taste, without looking at the label.
fact: The word comes from French, where it once meant the servant in charge of a household's supplies and drink.

name: Barista
description: Makes coffee on a professional machine, adjusts the grind and the temperature for each kind of bean and draws latte art on the milk foam. A good barista knows not only espresso but also the alternative brewing methods.
fact: World barista championships are judged not only on how the drink tastes but also on technique and presentation.

name: Pastry chef
description: Creates cakes, pastries and other desserts, combining exact recipes with decorative artistry. Works with chocolate, cream and fondant, and for elaborate wedding cakes sometimes assembles tiered constructions by hand.
fact: Professional pastry chefs weigh almost every ingredient on scales rather than measuring in cups and spoons, for the sake of accuracy.

name: Baker
description: Mixes dough and bakes bread and other baked goods, often starting work in the middle of the night so that the shelves are full by morning. Watches the temperature and humidity in the oven and how the yeast dough behaves at every stage.
fact: Baking bread on a sourdough starter without yeast goes back thousands of years and is still alive in many bakeries.

name: Farmer
description: Grows grain and vegetables or raises livestock, supplying towns and markets with food. The work depends on the season and the weather, and a modern farmer often combines physical labour with running machinery and the farm's finances.
fact: Yields and weather make farming one of the least predictable trades — much of it depends on things nobody can control.

name: Fisherman
description: Catches fish and seafood with nets, seines or rods, working on fishing boats or from the shore. A professional has to know the habits of the fish, the seasonal migrations and the rules that limit catches in different waters.
fact: Commercial fishing on the open sea counts as one of the most dangerous jobs there is, because of storms and the distance from help.

name: Miner
description: Extracts coal, ore and other minerals deep underground, working in darkness and cramped spaces with the constant risk of collapse and gas. Uses heavy machinery and ventilation systems, but the work is still among the most physically punishing there is.
fact: Miners used to take a canary down the shaft: the bird reacted to dangerous gas before people did, and today gas detectors do the job.

name: Welder
description: Joins metal parts with a welding machine, melting the edges to create a solid seam. Works in a mask to shield the eyes from the flash of the arc and from sparks, and a good welder keeps the seam straight even in an awkward position.
fact: The bright light of a welding arc and its ultraviolet can burn the eyes without a mask — welders call the injury arc eye.

name: Electrician
description: Lays wiring, fits sockets, distribution boards and lighting, and puts right faults in the electrical systems of homes and businesses. The work demands strict safety discipline, because a mistake can mean a shock or a fire.
fact: Before starting work an electrician always checks with a tester that there is no voltage in the circuit, even if the supply should be off.

name: Plumber
description: Fits and repairs pipes, taps, toilets and heating systems, clearing leaks and blockages. Often works in cramped conditions — under a sink or in a tiny service cupboard — and has to find the source of the problem fast.
fact: The English word plumber goes back to the Latin plumbum, lead: in ancient Rome water pipes were made of exactly that.

name: Construction worker
description: Puts up houses, roads and other structures, working with concrete, brick and reinforcement at the various stages of a build. The trade brings together many narrow specialities, from bricklayer to crane operator, under a site foreman.
fact: A hard hat on site is not for show — even a small object falling from a height can cause a serious injury.

name: Architect
description: Designs buildings and city spaces, combining engineering calculations with beauty and comfort for the people who will use them. Works on drawings and 3D models, then follows the project on site to make sure it is built as designed.
fact: Building the Sydney Opera House ran years longer and cost far more than the original design had allowed for.

name: Engineer
description: Designs and calculates technical systems, from bridges to engines, applying the laws of physics and mathematics to practical problems. There are many specialities: civil, aerospace, software and plenty more besides.
fact: The word engineer goes back to the Latin ingenium, natural wit or ingenuity, and once described the makers of siege machines.

name: Programmer
description: Writes code for websites, apps and other software, turning business problems into working algorithms. Much of the time goes not into writing code but into finding and fixing mistakes in it — the ones everyone calls bugs.
fact: The famous note about the first actual bug dates from 1947, when a moth was found stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer.

name: Cybersecurity specialist
description: Protects companies' computer systems and data from break-ins, viruses and leaks, finding weak points before attackers do. Some work on the defensive side, others as ethical hackers hired by a company to look for holes in its systems.
fact: Looking for vulnerabilities legally, for a reward paid by the company, is known as bug bounty hunting.

name: Designer
description: Creates the visual look of products, websites, packaging or interiors, combining beauty with ease of use. Works with colour, type and composition, and often backs up decisions not only with taste but with research on users.
fact: The branch that deals with how interfaces work and feel, not just how they look, is called UX design.

name: Tattoo artist
description: Puts permanent designs on skin with a tattoo machine that drives ink under the top layer. Before a session, agrees the sketch and the placement with the client, and afterwards explains how to look after a fresh tattoo while it heals.
fact: Some of the oldest known tattoos are on the body of the ice mummy Ötzi, a man who lived more than five thousand years ago.

name: Hairdresser
description: Cuts, styles and colours hair and looks after a client's whole look, matching it to the shape of the face and what the person wants. Beyond the cutting technique, listening and keeping a conversation going through a long session matters too.
fact: In the old days barbers also pulled teeth and did minor surgery — which is where the red and white pole outside barber shops comes from.

name: Make-up artist
description: Creates make-up for everyday looks, photo shoots and formal occasions, choosing colours and techniques to suit the client's skin and features. Often works alongside a photographer or stylist at fashion shows and film shoots.
fact: On film productions make-up artists often build not only beautiful faces but aged or battle-worn looks, using silicone appliances.

name: Model
description: Shows clothes and looks on the catwalks of fashion shows, in advertising and at photo shoots for magazines and brands. The job needs more than looks: posture, changing expression on cue and slipping into a new character within minutes.
fact: A model casting usually involves going through a portfolio — a selection of the model's best photographs in different looks and styles.

name: Actor
description: Plays roles in theatre, film and television, turning into different characters and carrying their emotions across to the audience. Prepares through reading the script, rehearsal and sometimes a serious change of appearance or way of speaking.
fact: A stage actor has to hold the whole part in memory: there are no second takes on stage, as there are in film.

name: Film director
description: Directs the shooting of a film and shapes its artistic vision, from working with the actors to choosing the framing, the light and the cut. Turns the script into a finished story on screen, coordinating dozens of people on set.
fact: By one account, the call for the camera to roll dates back to the days when film cameras were started by a mechanical drive.

name: Stunt performer
description: Performs the dangerous stunts in films in place of the actors — fights, falls, car chases and fires — rehearsing every movement carefully for safety. Uses harnesses, mats and protective gear hidden from the camera.
fact: Some stunt performers specialise in one kind of stunt only, fire work or car work for instance, honing that one skill for years.

name: Photographer
description: Photographs people, events and objects, building composition, light and the moment so that the frame tells a story. Works both in a studio with artificial light and outdoors, adapting to the natural light and the weather.
fact: Before digital cameras, photographers developed film by hand in a darkroom, using special chemical solutions.

name: Journalist
description: Gathers information, conducts interviews and writes for newspapers, websites or television, trying to check the facts against several independent sources. Often works to tight deadlines, especially when covering something happening right now.
fact: Checking every fact against at least two independent sources is one of the basic principles of journalistic ethics.

name: Television presenter
description: Presents television programmes — news, shows or live broadcasts — holding the viewer's attention with voice, pace and the ability to improvise when the technology misbehaves. Works from an autocue and a script, but has to be able to step away from both.
fact: The text on an autocue runs in front of the camera, so the presenter seems to speak without notes while looking straight into the lens.

name: Blogger
description: Creates text, photos and video on a particular subject for an audience on social media, anything from travel to personal finance. Beyond the creative part, handles editing, promotion and talking to followers, turning all of it into a full-time job.
fact: Many successful bloggers started as amateurs and only over time turned a hobby into their main source of income.

name: Streamer
description: Broadcasts live — games, conversation or creative work — talking to viewers in the chat in real time. Success depends heavily on streaming regularly and on holding an audience's attention for hours at a time.
fact: Donations and viewer subscriptions are one of the main ways streamers earn on platforms such as Twitch.

name: Esports player
description: Competes professionally in video games as part of a team, spending hours in training on reactions and coordinated tactics. Plays in tournaments with prize money, often broadcast online to a very large audience.
fact: The biggest esports tournaments now take place in arenas in front of a live crowd, just like ordinary sporting events.

name: DJ
description: Picks and mixes tracks into a single dance set, holding the room with changes of tempo and mood. Works with vinyl records, CD players or digital decks, and a good DJ reads a crowd better than any ready-made playlist.
fact: The trick of moving a record back and forth under the needle for a rhythmic sound is called scratching.

name: Conductor
description: Leads an orchestra or choir without saying a word: the hands and the baton alone set the tempo, the dynamics and the character of the performance. Before a concert comes long rehearsal, drawing dozens of musicians into one sound.
fact: A conductor normally stands with their back to the audience, because every gesture is aimed at the orchestra, not the public.

name: Ballerina
description: Dances roles in classical ballet, training for years on flexibility, stamina and the ability to dance for long stretches on the tips of the toes in pointe shoes. Almost every ballerina has years of daily hours at the barre behind her, from early childhood.
fact: Pointe shoes — the stiff ballet shoes — are fitted individually by each dancer, who sometimes breaks a new pair in before a performance.

name: Clown
description: Makes an audience laugh with tricks, mime and absurd situations, often without a single word, relying only on face and gesture. Works in the circus, at children's parties and in street shows, building one bright, recognisable character.
fact: A clown's make-up counts as a personal signature: many performers keep the face they once invented unchanged for years.

name: Magician
description: Performs tricks with vanishing objects, cards and levitation, giving the audience the sense of a real miracle. Behind the apparent magic lie months of practice in sleight of hand, misdirection and the exact timing of every movement.
fact: Magicians do not give away one another's secrets — an unwritten rule the profession has kept for decades.

name: Animal trainer
description: Teaches animals to follow commands and perform tricks, building trust through patience and constant practice. Works with all kinds of species, from dogs and horses to big cats, taking account of the habits and character of each individual animal.
fact: Modern training increasingly relies on positive reinforcement with treats rather than on compulsion.

name: Writer
description: Writes novels, short stories or non-fiction, turning ideas into coherent text that holds a reader from the first page to the last. The road from idea to finished book often takes months or even years of rewriting and revision.
fact: Many well-known writers stuck strictly to a daily writing ritual, working only at the same hour of the day, for instance.

name: Translator
description: Renders speech or written text from one language into another, trying to carry over not just the words but the meaning, the tone and the cultural context. Simultaneous interpreters in a booth follow a speaker with almost no delay, as the talk goes on.
fact: Simultaneous interpreting takes such concentration that interpreters in the booth normally swap over every 20 to 30 minutes.

name: Teacher
description: Teaches schoolchildren one or several subjects, prepares lessons and marks exercise books, and along the way helps children find an interest in learning. Beyond lessons, handles pastoral work, after-school activities and talking to parents.
fact: Different countries have their own days in honour of teachers — in Russia, for example, it falls on 5 October.

name: Professor
description: Teaches at a university and at the same time runs their own research, publishing papers and supervising the work of students and doctoral candidates. The title of professor is usually granted for years of recognised contribution to research and teaching.
fact: The word professor means different things in different countries: in some it is the highest academic rank, in others simply a university teaching post.

name: Librarian
description: Organises books and other materials, helps visitors find the edition they need and keeps track of the library's holdings. A modern librarian also deals with electronic catalogues and digital archives, not only with paper books.
fact: The Dewey library classification, devised in the 19th century, is still used in many libraries around the world to arrange books by subject.

name: Archaeologist
description: Studies the life of ancient people from objects, buildings and burials found in excavations, rebuilding a picture of the past from the smallest details. The work combines field expeditions with painstaking laboratory processing of the finds.
fact: Howard Carter found the tomb of Tutankhamun in 1922, after several years of fruitless digging in the Valley of the Kings.

name: Palaeontologist
description: Studies the fossil remains of dinosaurs and other ancient organisms to reconstruct what life on Earth looked like millions of years ago. The finds are often only fragments of bone, from which the scientist rebuilds the whole creature.
fact: Many dinosaur skeletons in museums are partly made of plaster copies of the missing bones, filling in around the real finds.

name: Astronomer
description: Studies stars, planets and other objects in the universe using telescopes and data from space missions, trying to work out the laws that govern the cosmos. Part of the job is nights at a telescope, but more and more astronomers analyse data at a computer.
fact: Not only professionals make important astronomical discoveries: amateurs with home telescopes regularly find new comets.

name: Nuclear physicist
description: Studies the structure of the atomic nucleus and what happens when it splits or fuses — knowledge that both energy production and medicine depend on. Works in laboratories and at large research facilities such as particle accelerators.
fact: Research in nuclear physics led not only to atomic power but also to radiotherapy in the treatment of cancer.

name: Chemist
description: Studies what substances are made of and how they react, creating new materials, medicines and technologies. Works in a laboratory with reagents and instruments, while some chemists work in production, checking the quality of the finished product.
fact: Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the periodic table so well that it predicted the properties of elements not yet discovered.

name: Oceanographer
description: Studies the currents, the depths and the inhabitants of the world ocean, explaining how the sea shapes the climate of the whole planet. Much of the work happens on expeditions aboard research ships, and with submersibles and instrumented buoys.
fact: The floor of the ocean is far less well explored than the surface of the Moon — much of it is still unstudied and unmapped in detail.

name: Volcanologist
description: Studies volcanoes and tries to predict eruptions from the composition of the gases, seismic activity and changes in the shape of the crater. To get samples of lava and gas, sometimes has to approach an active crater in a heat-proof suit.
fact: Some volcanologists have died while observing eruptions — the field remains one of the most dangerous in science.

name: Meteorologist
description: Watches the atmosphere and puts together weather forecasts, analysing data from satellites, radar and weather stations around the world. Besides the daily forecast, meteorologists warn of approaching hurricanes, storms and other dangerous events.
fact: Regular weather reports first went out by telegraph in the 19th century, laying the foundation of today's weather services.

name: Geologist
description: Studies the structure of the earth's crust, rocks and minerals, and looks for deposits of useful raw materials. Spends a lot of time on field expeditions with a hammer and a compass, reading the history of the Earth in the layers of rock.
fact: From the layers of sedimentary rock and the composition of minerals, geologists can reconstruct events that happened millions of years ago.

name: Psychologist
description: Helps people make sense of their feelings, relationships and difficult decisions through conversation, without prescribing medication — unlike a psychiatrist. Works with individuals, couples or groups, using a range of therapeutic approaches.
fact: Psychologist and psychiatrist are different professions: a psychiatrist has a medical degree and can prescribe drugs, while a psychologist usually cannot.

name: Pharmacist
description: Dispenses medicines in a pharmacy, advises on dosage and on how drugs interact, and sometimes prepares the preparations personally. Knows chemistry and pharmacology well enough to spot a dangerous combination of several drugs in time.
fact: In the old days apothecaries made most medicines by hand, mixing powders and tinctures right behind the counter.

name: Nurse
description: Cares for patients in a hospital or clinic: gives injections and changes dressings, monitors their condition and carries out the doctor's orders. Often it is the nurse who spends more time with a patient than anyone else in the hospital.
fact: Florence Nightingale, one of the founders of modern nursing, became famous for caring for the wounded during the Crimean War.

name: Paramedic
description: Gives emergency medical care on call-outs and on the way to hospital, often in the first and most important minutes after an injury or an attack. Has to decide fast, under stress, with only the equipment carried in the vehicle.
fact: Emergency medics talk about the golden hour — the first hour after a serious injury, when prompt care does most to improve the chances of survival.

name: Pathologist
description: Examines tissue and organs to refine a diagnosis or establish a cause of death, working where medicine meets forensic science. Much of the job is not autopsies but studying tissue under a microscope to diagnose living patients.
fact: To see tissue under a microscope, it is cut into an extremely thin slice and stained with special dyes — otherwise almost nothing shows.

name: Obstetrician
description: Delivers babies and monitors the condition of mother and child at every stage of pregnancy, deciding on urgent intervention when complications appear. The work needs calm and quick reactions, because a birth does not always follow the plan.
fact: For centuries many cultures had a separate, usually female profession of midwives, who helped at births without formal medical training.

name: Football manager
description: Works out the tactics for a match, trains the players and decides on the line-up and the substitutions during the game itself. Beyond football knowledge, needs some grasp of psychology to keep a squad motivated through a whole season.
fact: Some managers have won major trophies with different clubs and national teams, proving that tactical thinking counts for more than one particular squad.

name: Footballer
description: Plays football for a club or a national team, spending years sharpening ball control, speed and tactical thinking on the pitch. A professional career usually begins in a youth academy and demands constant training.
fact: Football is called the most popular sport in the world — in one form or another it is played in most countries.

name: Boxer
description: Fights in the ring under strict rules, using only the fists, and wins by knockout or on the judges' points. Preparing for a bout means months of work on stamina, reaction speed and defensive technique.
fact: Boxers are divided strictly into weight classes, so that opponents are of roughly equal body mass going into a fight.

name: Formula 1 driver
description: Drives a Formula 1 car at very high speed, taking huge physical loads through the fast corners. Beyond reactions and stamina, a driver needs a fine feel for the car and constant radio contact with the team.
fact: Between the heat in the cockpit and the loads during a race, Formula 1 drivers lose a noticeable amount of weight through sweat.

name: Mountaineer
description: Climbs mountain peaks, including the highest in the world, dealing with thin air, cold and the risk of avalanche. Serious summits usually take more than one day and call for acclimatisation and gear built for extreme conditions.
fact: At great altitude the air is so thin that climbers on summits like Everest often use bottled oxygen.

name: Commercial diver
description: Carries out work underwater, from inspecting ships' hulls and submerged structures to search and rescue. Uses equipment with an air supply and has to understand the physiology of diving in order to avoid decompression sickness.
fact: At great depth divers breathe not ordinary air but helium mixtures — otherwise nitrogen under pressure produces something close to drunkenness.

name: Rescue worker
description: Saves people in fires, floods, collapses and other emergencies, often being first on the scene. The work needs physical fitness, the ability to size up a situation fast and command of a whole range of rescue equipment.
fact: Rescue work often takes place in conditions considered unsafe even for specially trained professionals.

name: Forest ranger
description: Watches over the state of the forest, fights illegal logging and poaching, and organises the planting of young trees and fire prevention. The work happens mostly outdoors, often a long way from any settlement.
fact: A ranger's duties often include counting wildlife — how many animals of each species live in the patch entrusted to them.

name: Ship's captain
description: Answers for the ship and the whole crew, decides on course, weather and the safety of the voyage, and carries full responsibility for how the trip ends. Reaching the bridge usually takes years of work in various posts at sea.
fact: By maritime tradition the captain is the last to leave a sinking ship, having made sure everyone else on board has got off safely.

name: Train driver
description: Drives the train, watches the signals and the state of the track, and answers for the safety of hundreds of passengers at once. The job demands concentration through a whole shift, because a heavy train's braking distance can run to hundreds of metres.
fact: The cab has a vigilance control system: the driver has to confirm periodically that all is well, or the train brakes by itself.

name: Long-haul trucker
description: Hauls freight over long distances, spending long hours and days at the wheel of a lorry, often in other cities and countries. The job takes stamina and planning a route around the compulsory rest stops.
fact: In many countries the law limits how long truckers may drive without a break, for the sake of road safety.

name: Taxi driver
description: Carries passengers around the city by car, knowing the routes well and able to find a way through traffic and diversions. Navigation apps and ride-hailing have changed the job a good deal, but knowing how to talk to passengers still matters.
fact: In London the drivers of the famous black cabs spend years preparing for the Knowledge, an exam that requires learning thousands of streets by heart.

name: Courier
description: Delivers parcels, food and documents to the addressee, moving around the city on foot, by bicycle, scooter or car. With the growth of online orders and food delivery the job has become one of the most common in big cities.
fact: Couriers on bicycles and scooters often get an order through dense city traffic faster than a car can.

name: Air traffic controller
description: Tracks aircraft in the air and on the ground, directing them so as to avoid collisions and keep take-offs and landings safe. The job demands unbroken concentration: a controller holds dozens of flights and their routes in mind at once.
fact: Controllers and pilots talk in a special standardised form of English, to avoid confusion over accents or terminology.

name: Flight attendant
description: Keeps passengers safe and comfortable on board, from the briefing before take-off to helping in an emergency. Beyond the service, has to be able to give first aid and organise an evacuation if something goes wrong.
fact: Before every flight the cabin crew attend a briefing and have to know the position of every emergency exit and piece of equipment by heart.

name: Diplomat
description: Represents the interests of their country abroad, conducts negotiations and helps settle disagreements between states by peaceful means. Works in embassies and consulates, and a large part of the career is usually spent overseas.
fact: Diplomatic immunity protects diplomats from arrest and trial in the host country — a custom known since antiquity.

name: Intelligence officer
description: Collects and analyses secret information in their country's interest, often working under a cover story — an invented biography and a front. Because of the secrecy, the details of real intelligence work usually surface only decades later, if at all.
fact: Most intelligence work is the analysis of open sources, not the spectacular covert operations that films like to show.

name: Bomb disposal technician
description: Finds and defuses mines, shells and other explosive devices, working with a jeweller's precision where the cost of a mistake is extremely high. Besides clearing mines, also puts up barriers and engineering works in wartime.
fact: There is a saying in the trade that in this job you only make one mistake — a way of describing the price of any slip.

name: Banker
description: Manages a bank's financial operations, from lending and deposits to large investment deals for companies. The profession covers many different lines of work, from serving ordinary customers at a branch to analysing whole markets.
fact: The word bank comes from the Italian banco, the bench or counter at which medieval money changers did their business.

name: Trader
description: Buys and sells shares, currency or other financial assets on the exchange, trying to make money on the difference in price. Decisions often have to be taken in seconds, so a trader must read news and price charts fast.
fact: A large share of exchange transactions today are made not by people but by automated algorithms, in fractions of a second.

name: Accountant
description: Keeps the record of a company's income, spending and taxes, making sure all the financial paperwork is in order and complies with the law. Accuracy and attention to detail matter especially here — an error in a return can mean a heavy fine.
fact: Double-entry bookkeeping, where every transaction is recorded in two accounts at once, has been known since the Italian Renaissance.

name: Estate agent
meta: helps people buy and sell homes
description: Helps clients buy, sell and rent property, knowing the prices in a district, the legal fine print of a deal and the state of the market. A good agent can find the right options and negotiate between seller and buyer.
fact: In valuing a home, agents look not only at floor area and condition but at things like the view from the window and the floor it is on.

name: Entrepreneur
description: Starts and grows a business of their own, taking on financial risk in the hope of profit from a new product or service. Beyond the idea, needs skill in managing people and money, and the ability to rework the plan when things go wrong.
fact: Many well-known companies started small — literally in the founders' garage, for instance — before growing into big business.

name: Priest
description: Leads services and religious rites and gives spiritual guidance to parishioners on matters of faith and of everyday life. Beyond the services, a priest is often involved in charity and in supporting members of the community in need.
fact: Different Christian denominations have different rules: Orthodoxy and Catholicism, for instance, settle the question of clerical marriage differently.

name: Jeweller
description: Makes and repairs jewellery from precious metals and stones, combining a craftsman's precision with artistic taste. Works on tiny details under magnification, and cutting a stone calls for special accuracy and years of experience.
fact: The brilliant cut, with its dozens of facets, is calculated to refract light and give a stone the maximum possible sparkle.

name: Blacksmith
description: Shapes metal by heating it in a forge and striking it with a hammer on the anvil, making tools, fittings and ornaments. The craft is one of the oldest in human history and is still in demand, from decorative ironwork to restoration.
fact: In the old days blacksmiths were often thought a little magical — turning a shapeless lump of metal into a finished object looked close to sorcery.

name: Joiner
description: Makes furniture, windows, doors and other things out of wood, working with saws, planes and other tools. A good carpenter knows the properties of different species of wood and can join pieces without a single nail.
fact: Some traditional wooden joints, the dovetail for instance, hold a structure firmly with no glue or nails at all.

name: Watchmaker
description: Assembles, adjusts and repairs watches, working with dozens of tiny parts of the movement under a magnifying glass. The trade calls for patience and a very steady hand, since an error of a fraction of a millimetre can stop the whole mechanism.
fact: A complicated mechanical watch can hold several hundred tiny parts, and the watchmaker has to know what each one is for.

name: Perfumer
description: Creates the fragrances for perfumes, blending dozens of natural and synthetic components in exact proportions. Much of the work rests on an extraordinarily trained sense of smell, able to tell apart and remember thousands of separate scents.
fact: Professional perfumers with an exceptional sense of smell are sometimes called a nose, from the French le nez.

name: Florist
description: Puts together bouquets and floral arrangements for celebrations, weddings and everyday gifts, knowing which flowers go together and how to care for them. Has to know which flowers last and which wilt quickly once they are cut.
fact: Cutting the stem properly, at an angle and under water, noticeably extends the life of cut flowers in a bouquet.

name: Beekeeper
description: Keeps bees and watches over the state of the hives, and harvests honey, wax and other products of the hive. The work calls for calm around a swarm and a good knowledge of how bees behave at different times of the year.
fact: Beekeepers use a smoker to fill the hive with smoke — it calms the bees and lowers the risk of being stung during an inspection.

name: Taster
description: Tastes food, drink or raw materials professionally, to judge their quality, their flavour and whether they meet production standards. The work rests on trained taste and smell, able to pick out the finest shades of flavour and aroma.
fact: Professional tasters often spit out what they are tasting rather than swallowing it, to keep their palate sensitive all day.

name: Tour guide
description: Leads tours around a city, a museum or a historic site, telling entertaining facts and bringing history alive for visitors. A good guide holds a group's attention and answers unexpected questions without glancing at any notes.
fact: In some countries, Italy for instance, official guides need a licence, awarded after an exam in history and art.

name: Croupier
description: Runs a gambling table in a casino — deals the cards, spins the roulette wheel and makes sure every rule is kept fairly. The job needs fast mental arithmetic and an unmoved face, however much a player is winning or losing.
fact: Cameras in the ceiling watch the tables and the croupiers themselves constantly — in casinos the system is called the eye in the sky.

name: Spy
description: Someone whose work is the covert gathering of information for a state or an organisation, often under a false name and a cover story. The job carries a high risk of exposure and demands an ability to keep secrets.
fact: Real intelligence work rarely resembles the films — most of it consists of routine analysis of open sources.

name: Fighter pilot
description: A military flier who handles a fast jet built for air combat and for destroying enemy targets. The job takes years of training, excellent physical condition and the ability to decide in fractions of a second.
fact: In sharp manoeuvres fighter pilots take g-forces several times the weight of their own body.

name: Sniper
description: A marksman trained specially to hit targets accurately at long range, often working alone or in a pair with a spotter. The work takes patience, camouflage and the ability to stay motionless for a long time.
fact: Snipers often lie in wait for hours, waiting for the single right moment to take a shot.

name: Paratrooper
description: A soldier in units meant to be delivered behind enemy lines by air, most often by parachute. Paratroopers go through intensive physical training and count as among the most combat-ready parts of an army.
fact: The first large-scale military parachute drops came into use as early as the 1930s.

name: Marine
meta: fights on land and from the sea
description: A soldier of the marines — the branch of the forces built for landing troops from ships and for fighting on the coast. Marines count as elite units in many of the armed forces of the world.
fact: Marines have existed as a separate branch of the forces for several centuries and serve in the armed forces of dozens of countries.

name: Tank crewman
description: A member of the crew of an armoured fighting vehicle, responsible for driving, aiming the gun or communications inside the tank. The work goes on in a tight, enclosed space and demands that the whole crew act as one.
fact: The crew of a modern tank usually numbers only three or four people, despite the imposing size of the machine.

name: Prison officer
description: An officer who maintains order and safety in places of detention and sees that inmates keep to the regime. The work takes self-control, an ability to defuse conflicts and strict adherence to procedure.
fact: An officer's duties often involve not only guarding but keeping track of inmates' movements throughout the day.

name: Bodyguard
description: A specialist responsible for the physical safety of the person being protected, from a politician to a celebrity. The work involves planning routes, assessing risks and constant readiness for the unexpected.
fact: Good bodyguards try to be as inconspicuous as possible rather than standing out in appearance, as films often show them.

name: Mercenary
description: Someone who takes part in armed conflict not out of conviction but for money, often on the side of a foreign state or a private company. The trade has been known since deep antiquity and still exists in various forms.
fact: International law defines the status of mercenaries in various ways, which often leaves them without the protection ordinary combatants have.

name: Special forces operator
description: A soldier of special forces units, who goes through exceptionally intensive training to carry out difficult and dangerous tasks. Such troops take part in reconnaissance, sabotage and counter-terrorist operations.
fact: In many countries only a small percentage of candidates get through selection for special forces units.

name: General practitioner
description: A general doctor, the first person people turn to for most illnesses. The GP makes the initial diagnosis, prescribes treatment and refers the patient on to a specialist where that is necessary.
fact: It is usually the GP who becomes the doctor a patient keeps going back to for many years running.

name: Paediatrician
description: A doctor specialising in children's health, from newborns to teenagers. The paediatrician follows a child's development, carries out check-ups and vaccinations, and treats childhood illnesses with age in mind.
fact: Paediatrics only took shape as a separate branch of medicine in the 19th century; before that children were treated by ordinary doctors.

name: Ophthalmologist
description: A doctor who diagnoses and treats diseases of the eye and the visual system. The ophthalmologist checks visual acuity, prescribes glasses and lenses, and treats conditions such as cataract and glaucoma.
fact: Many eye diseases have no symptoms in their early stages, which is why ophthalmologists recommend regular check-ups.

name: Cardiologist
description: A doctor specialising in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the heart and the blood vessels. The cardiologist reads cardiograms and follows patients with hypertension and other chronic conditions of the cardiovascular system.
fact: Cardiovascular disease remains one of the main reasons people see a doctor anywhere in the world.

name: Oncologist
description: A doctor who diagnoses and treats cancer. The oncologist determines the type and stage of a tumour and works out a plan of treatment together with surgeons, chemotherapists and radiologists.
fact: Modern oncology increasingly relies on methods of early detection, which raise the chances of successful treatment.

name: Dermatologist
description: A doctor specialising in diseases of the skin, hair and nails. The dermatologist treats common problems such as acne and eczema as well as more serious conditions, including growths on the skin.
fact: Skin is the largest organ of the human body, which is why dermatology covers a very wide range of conditions.

name: Gynaecologist
description: A doctor concerned with the health of the female reproductive system at every stage of life. The gynaecologist carries out preventive examinations, follows pregnancies and treats a wide range of conditions.
fact: Regular visits to a gynaecologist count as one of the key elements of preventive medicine for women.

name: Psychiatrist
description: A doctor who diagnoses and treats mental disorders with medication and other medical methods. Unlike a psychologist, a psychiatrist has a medical degree and the right to prescribe drugs.
fact: Psychiatry only began to take shape as an independent field of medicine at the end of the 18th and the start of the 19th century.

name: Anaesthetist
description: A doctor responsible for keeping the patient free of pain and for monitoring their vital signs during surgery. The safety of an operation depends directly on how precisely the anaesthetist works.
fact: Modern anaesthesia makes possible operations that in the 19th century were simply out of the question because of pain and shock.

name: Orthopaedic surgeon
description: A doctor who diagnoses and treats diseases and injuries of bones, joints, ligaments and muscles. The orthopaedic surgeon deals with fractures, curvature of the spine and the aftermath of sporting injuries.
fact: Many orthopaedic surgeons work closely with sports teams, helping athletes recover from injury.

name: Speech therapist
description: A specialist who diagnoses and corrects speech disorders in children and adults. The speech therapist helps with delayed speech development, problems of pronunciation and the consequences of certain injuries.
fact: Work with a speech therapist is often built around play, especially in sessions with small children.

name: Dietitian
description: A specialist who helps people adjust their diet with their state of health, their goals and their way of life in mind. Dietitians work both with people who want to lose weight and with patients who need a therapeutic diet.
fact: A dietitian's advice always rests on the individual characteristics of the person, not on universal diets.

name: Massage therapist
description: A specialist who works on the body with the hands to relieve muscle tension, improve circulation or aid recovery after injury. Massage therapists work in sports clubs as well as in medical settings.
fact: Massage was used as a method of treatment and recovery in the ancient civilisations of China, Egypt and Greece.

name: Physiotherapist
description: A specialist who helps patients recover mobility and bodily function after injury, surgery or illness, using physical methods of treatment. Physiotherapy often combines exercise, massage and specialised equipment.
fact: A physiotherapy rehabilitation programme is always drawn up individually, around the patient's particular injury.

name: Web designer
description: A specialist responsible for the look and the usability of websites and web applications. The web designer works out the placement of elements, the colour scheme and the fonts so that a site is convenient and pleasant to use.
fact: Good web design nearly always goes unnoticed by the user — it simply does not get in the way of the task.

name: Data analyst
description: A specialist who collects, processes and interprets data to help a business take well-founded decisions. The data analyst works with spreadsheets, databases and tools for visualising results.
fact: A large part of a data analyst's work goes not into analysis but into cleaning and preparing the data itself.

name: AI specialist
description: A specialist who develops and trains algorithms able to perform tasks that normally call for human intelligence. The field involves work with neural networks, machine learning and the processing of data.
fact: Many modern artificial intelligence systems are trained on vast bodies of data gathered from open sources.

name: Game designer
description: A specialist who works out the rules, the mechanics and the overall structure of a video game, from the level of difficulty to the balance between characters. The game designer is responsible for making play both engaging and coherent.
fact: A game designer often tests their own levels hundreds of times to find the right balance of difficulty.

name: Software tester
description: A specialist who checks programs and applications for errors and inconsistencies before they are released. The tester reproduces the actions of an ordinary user, trying to find the weak points of the product.
fact: An error found by a tester in program code is commonly called a bug — the English word for an insect.

name: System administrator
description: A specialist responsible for setting up, running and securing an organisation's computer networks and servers. The system administrator fixes technical faults and makes sure the infrastructure keeps working without interruption.
fact: Many system administrators solve part of the problems remotely, without physically going near the computer in question.

name: Copywriter
description: A specialist who writes text for advertising, websites and marketing materials, with the job of catching attention and convincing the reader. The copywriter combines a command of language with an understanding of the audience's psychology.
fact: The copywriter's trade has grown noticeably with the rise of internet advertising and social media over recent decades.

name: Screenwriter
description: The author who creates the plot, the dialogue and the structure of a film, a series or a play. The screenwriter thinks through the characters' arcs and builds the drama so as to hold the audience from beginning to end.
fact: Work on the script of a big film often takes several years and goes through dozens of drafts.

name: Illustrator
meta: draws pictures for books and publications
description: An artist who creates images for books, magazines, advertising or digital products. The illustrator works both with traditional materials and in specialised graphics software on a computer.
fact: Many well-known children's books are remembered first of all for the recognisable style of their illustrator.

name: Animator
meta: brings characters to life on screen
description: A specialist who creates the movement of characters and objects in cartoons, films or video games. The animator thinks through every frame so that the motion looks alive and natural.
fact: For a single second of classic hand-drawn animation, an artist often has to draw more than a dozen frames.

name: Stand-up comedian
description: A performer who stands in front of an audience with comic monologues, jokes and observations about life. The comedian sharpens the material in live shows, gradually turning notes into a polished stage act.
fact: Many comedians spend years testing the same joke in small clubs before showing it to a wide audience.

name: Singer
description: A performer whose profession is to render music with the voice, whether on the concert stage, in the studio or on a recording. Singers work in every genre, from opera to pop music.
fact: Professional singers spend years training their breathing and their vocal cords to stand up to long concert tours.

name: Musician
description: Someone who plays a musical instrument professionally — solo, in an orchestra or as part of a band. A musician may perform live, record in the studio or teach others how to play the instrument.
fact: Many professional musicians master not one but several instruments over the course of a career.

name: Composer
description: The author of musical works, from songs and symphonies to soundtracks for films and games. The composer thinks out the melody, the harmony and the arrangement, often working closely with the performers.
fact: Many film composers write the music before they have seen the finished film, going only by the script and a rough cut.

name: Producer
description: A specialist responsible for the organisation and the creative side of making an album, a film or a show, from the idea to the final result. The producer picks the team, controls the budget and watches over the quality of the end product.
fact: In the music industry the producer often shapes the final sound of an album no less than the performer does.

name: Sound engineer
description: A specialist responsible for recording, processing and mixing sound in music, in film or at live concerts. The sound engineer watches over the quality of the sound and the balance between the different sources.
fact: How the public hears a finished recording or a live concert depends directly on the quality of the sound engineer's work.

name: Cinematographer
meta: shoots the images for a film
description: A specialist responsible for the visual construction of the shot, the light and the movement of the camera in a film. The cinematographer works hand in hand with the director to turn the idea of the film into concrete images.
fact: The choice of lens and lighting can change the mood of one and the same scene completely.

name: Film editor
meta: assembles the film from the footage
description: A specialist who assembles the final version of a film, a series or a clip out of the footage shot, building the pace and the logic of the story. The edit largely decides how the audience will take the finished story.
fact: Experienced editors can change the sense of a scene completely just by reordering the shots.

name: Stylist
description: A specialist who chooses the clothes, the accessories and the whole look for a shoot, a show or an individual client. The stylist follows the trends and knows how to bring out a person's individuality through appearance.
fact: On a big fashion shoot a stylist often handles dozens of complete outfits in the course of a single day.

name: Interior designer
description: A specialist who works out the layout, the finishes and the furnishing of homes and commercial spaces. The interior designer thinks not only about beauty but about comfort, lighting and how the space will function.
fact: Good interior design takes account not only of how a room looks but of how a person will move around it.

name: Tennis player
description: An athlete who competes in tennis, the game with racket and ball in which opponents hit the ball back and forth over a net. Professional players travel the world for years, taking part in tournaments at every level.
fact: In professional tennis the score in a game is traditionally counted in unusual numbers — fifteen, thirty, forty.

name: Gymnast
description: An athlete competing in gymnastics, a discipline that combines strength, flexibility and artistry on various pieces of apparatus. Gymnasts begin training in early childhood, because the sport demands unusual suppleness.
fact: Gymnastics routines are judged on several criteria at once, from the difficulty of the elements to the cleanness of execution.

name: Swimmer
description: An athlete who competes in swimming over various distances and in various strokes, from freestyle to butterfly. Professional swimmers spend several hours a day training in the pool.
fact: The different strokes — front crawl, breaststroke, butterfly and backstroke — each call for a completely different technique.

name: Skier
description: An athlete competing in skiing disciplines, from endurance racing to fast descents from the mountains. Skiing brings together many different branches, each demanding its own physical preparation and technique.
fact: Skiing covers both flat endurance racing and fast mountain descents — disciplines with entirely different demands.

name: Figure skater
description: An athlete competing in figure skating, a sport that combines difficult jumps and spins with the artistry and musicality of the programme. Skaters train from early childhood, polishing their technique over years.
fact: A skater's score is made up of the technical difficulty of the elements and the artistic impression of the programme.

name: Ice hockey player
description: An athlete who plays ice hockey, a fast team game played on the ice with sticks. Hockey players combine speed, physical contact and accuracy in shooting at the opponents' goal, all at once.
fact: Hockey players change on the ice very often — a shift usually lasts less than a minute, because the game is so intense.

name: Basketball player
description: An athlete who plays basketball, a team game in which the aim is to throw the ball into the opponents' hoop. Players combine height, speed and accuracy in shooting, and the game demands coordinated team tactics.
fact: Basketball was originally invented as an indoor game for the cold season, when playing sport outdoors was not an option.

name: Baseball player
description: An athlete who plays baseball, a team game with a bat and a ball, particularly popular in the United States, Japan and Latin America. Each position on the team calls for its own particular skills, from pitching to batting.
fact: Baseball is called the national game of the United States, though in television popularity it long ago lost out to American football.

name: Rugby player
description: An athlete who plays rugby, a contact team game with an oval ball where strength, stamina and team cohesion count for a great deal. Rugby players often play without the protective gear worn in American football.
fact: In rugby the ball may only be passed to team-mates backwards or sideways, never forwards.

name: Personal trainer
description: A specialist who helps people build a training programme suited to their goals, from losing weight to putting on muscle. The trainer watches the technique of each exercise and keeps the client coming back regularly.
fact: A good personal trainer always draws up the programme individually, taking account of the client's fitness and state of health.

name: Yoga instructor
description: A specialist who teaches people the practice of yoga — a system of exercises, breathing techniques and meditation that came from ancient India. The instructor watches that the poses are done correctly and adapts the practice to each student's level.
fact: Yoga as a spiritual and physical practice began in India several thousand years ago.

name: Mathematician
description: A scientist who studies numbers, shapes, structures and the relations between them at an abstract level. A mathematician's work can be theoretical or applied — from proving theorems to calculations in engineering.
fact: Some mathematical problems stay unsolved for decades, despite the efforts of the best minds in the world.

name: Biologist
description: A scientist who studies living organisms — their structure, their behaviour, their development and their interaction with the environment. Biology brings together many branches, from the study of cells to whole ecosystems.
fact: Modern biology is closely interwoven with chemistry and physics, especially at the level of molecular processes.

name: Geneticist
description: A scientist who investigates genes and the mechanisms of heredity in living organisms. Geneticists study how traits pass from one generation to the next and work on understanding the causes of inherited disease.
fact: Working out the structure of DNA in the middle of the 20th century transformed the understanding of heredity.

name: Ecologist
description: A specialist who studies how living organisms interact with one another and with their surroundings. Ecologists assess the state of natural areas, study the consequences of human activity and work out measures to protect nature.
fact: The word ecology comes from a Greek root meaning house or dwelling place.

name: Sociologist
description: A scientist who studies how society is arranged: social groups, institutions and the behaviour of people within them. Sociologists run surveys, analyse statistics and pick out the patterns in public life.
fact: One of the sociologist's basic tools remains the mass survey, which reveals the mood of large groups of people.

name: Economist
description: A specialist who studies how a society produces, distributes and consumes resources and goods. Economists analyse markets, forecast trends and advise businesses or government bodies.
fact: Economic forecasts often diverge from reality, because the market is also shaped by the behaviour of people themselves.

name: Historian
description: A scholar who studies events of the past on the basis of documents, artefacts and other sources. The historian not only gathers facts but tries to understand the causes and the consequences of what happened in each era.
fact: A large part of a historian's work goes not into archives full of rare finds but into the painstaking reading of documents.

name: Philosopher
description: A thinker who works on fundamental questions of existence, knowledge, morality and the meaning of life. Philosophy does not always supply ready answers, but it teaches how to ask the right questions and build a rigorous argument.
fact: Many modern sciences — from physics to psychology — grew historically out of philosophy.

name: Carpenter
description: A craftsman who makes and installs wooden structures, from the frames of houses to furniture and staircases. Carpentry demands accuracy, a knowledge of the properties of timber and skill with both hand and power tools.
fact: Carpentry is one of the oldest trades in human history, known since the first wooden buildings were put up.

name: Painter and decorator
description: A tradesman who paints and finishes walls, ceilings and other surfaces inside and outside buildings. The painter prepares the surface, chooses the materials and lays the coating on in an even layer.
fact: The quality of a paint job depends less on the painting itself than on how thoroughly the surface was prepared beforehand.

name: Tiler
description: A tradesman who specialises in laying ceramic tiles on floors and walls — in bathrooms, kitchens and other rooms. The work calls for exact measurement and care, so that the joints and the pattern line up.
fact: An experienced tiler lays the pattern out dry beforehand, to avoid awkward cuts at the edges of a wall.

name: Car mechanic
description: A specialist who diagnoses and fixes faults in cars, from the engine to the electronics. The mechanic deals with the computerised systems of modern vehicles as well as with classic mechanical assemblies.
fact: Modern cars are increasingly diagnosed not only by hand but with special computer equipment.

name: Fitter
description: A worker who shapes metal by hand and by machine, and who assembles and repairs mechanisms. The trade covers a wide range of work, from servicing equipment to making precise parts.
fact: The fitter's trade is traditionally counted as one of the basic skilled jobs in mechanical engineering.

name: Lathe operator
description: A worker who makes parts by rotating a workpiece on a lathe and cutting it with a tool. The turner can produce precise cylindrical components for all sorts of different mechanisms.
fact: The lathe is one of the oldest kinds of machine tool, known since antiquity, though back then it was turned by hand.

name: Seamstress
description: A craftswoman who makes and repairs clothes and textile goods with a sewing machine and by hand. Seamstresses work both in mass-production factories and in small workshops making things to order.
fact: The arrival of the sewing machine in the 19th century made sewing clothes many times faster than doing it by hand.

name: Tailor
description: A craftsman who makes clothes to the customer's own measurements, from everyday suits to complicated bespoke pieces. The tailor takes the measurements, chooses the cloth and works until the garment fits perfectly.
fact: Making a classic suit to order with an experienced tailor can take more than a week of painstaking work.

name: Brewer
description: A craftsman who makes beer, from the choice of malt and hops to control over fermentation and maturing. The brewer decides the taste, the strength and the aroma of the finished drink at every stage of production.
fact: Brewing is one of humanity's oldest crafts, known from deep antiquity in civilisations all over the world.

name: Winemaker
description: A specialist in charge of the whole process of making wine, from growing the grapes to fermentation, ageing and blending. The quality of a wine depends greatly on climate, soil and the winemaker's skill.
fact: Many winemakers spend years watching one particular plot of vineyard to understand its character and its potential.

name: Butcher
description: A specialist who cuts up carcasses and prepares meat for sale or for further processing. The butcher understands animal anatomy and knows how to break a carcass down into the different cuts.
fact: Different peoples have their own traditional schemes for cutting up a carcass, which differ in the number of cuts.

name: Waiter
description: A member of staff in a place that serves food, taking orders from customers and bringing dishes and drinks to the table. The waiter also helps guests choose and looks after their comfort throughout the visit.
fact: In expensive restaurants waiters often go through training that covers the details of serving dishes and the rules for pairing them with drinks.

name: Street cleaner
description: A worker responsible for cleanliness and order on an assigned patch, from sweeping the paths to clearing snow in winter. The work is especially noticeable between seasons, when pedestrians' safety depends on it directly.
fact: In snowy cities it is largely the work of street cleaners that decides how safe the pavements turn out to be in winter.

name: Gardener
description: A specialist who looks after gardens, parks and plantings, from putting plants in the ground to mowing lawns and pruning trees. The gardener understands the needs of different species and the seasonal rhythm of caring for them.
fact: Experienced gardeners plan their planting several years ahead, thinking about how the plants will look at different ages.

name: Landscape designer
meta: designs the look of open spaces
description: A specialist who plans the layout and the appearance of open spaces — parks, squares and private grounds. The landscape designer brings plants, paths and small structures together into a single composition.
fact: A good landscape scheme takes account not only of beauty but of how the site will look in each season of the year.

name: Nanny
description: A specialist who looks after children while the parents are away, from feeding and walks to games and activities that help them develop. The nanny takes on part of the daily care of a child, and sometimes elements of early teaching.
fact: In many families the nanny becomes someone the child trusts no less than close relatives.

name: Postman
description: A postal worker who delivers letters, newspapers, parcels and notices along an assigned round. Despite the rise of email, the job remains in demand thanks to parcels and official documents.
fact: Postal services in various countries have existed for centuries, though the ways of delivering mail have changed enormously.
